key_insight: State-augmented reinforcement learning controls synthetic jets around elliptical cylinders, achieving complete vortex-shedding suppression and up to 32.2% drag reduction at aspect ratio Ar = 0.1.
engineering_relevance: The approach could enable adaptive drag reduction and wake stabilization for slender bodies with challenging flow dynamics.
method: Learn synthetic-jet control strategies using deep reinforcement learning.
Evaluate control across elliptical-cylinder aspect ratios from 1 to 0.1.
Enrich dynamic state features and apply Kalman filtering for the slender Ar = 0.1 case.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports drag reductions of 13.4%, 20.1%, 26.88%, and 30.37% at Ar = 1, 0.75, 0.5, and 0.25, respectively, and a maximum of 32.2% at Ar = 0.1 with complete vortex-shedding suppression.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify actuation energy costs or experimental validation, leaving net efficiency and practical deployment uncertain.
paper_title: State-augmented deep reinforcement learning for active flow control around an elliptical cylinder
